correctness.rationale: A positive accepted binary index implies acceptance of each nonzero canonical suffix, yielding b_(q2^m+r)<=b_r. Splitting any length-2^m factor at the aligned block boundary proves the prefix maximizes weight. Accepted positive l-bit numbers correspond bijectively to compositions of l-1 using tiles 1,2, counted by Fibonacci F_l; including b_0=1 gives F_(m+2). The binary prefix 101 forces zero blocks of arbitrary dyadic size. Consecutive window weights differ by <=1, so exactly F_(m+2)+1 Parikh vectors occur. Independent generators and exhaustive finite windows through m=11 were checked, but not used to infer infinity.

value.rationale: Abelian complexity counts the number of distinguishable jumbled factor profiles. The exact formula F_(m+2)+1 across every power-of-two length is a natural infinite-scale quantitative invariant, and the stronger coordinatewise suffix-closure property supplies structural explanation. It is unbounded with Fibonacci-in-exponent growth unlike several familiar bounded-complexity automatic words. No arbitrary finite cutoff, parameter renaming or routine table increment is involved.
